rule.title: Suspicious Windows Service Tampering
rule.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), frack113 , X__Junior (Nextron Systems)

es.summary: Se ejecutó net, sc, PowerShell, wmic o PsService para detener, pausar, deshabilitar o eliminar un servicio crítico (antivirus, EDR, backup, base de datos o VSS). Es un paso habitual de los scripts de ransomware antes del cifrado.
es.what_it_detects: Creación de procesos de net.exe, net1.exe, sc.exe, wmic.exe, PsService, powershell.exe, pwsh.exe o PowerShell ISE (por Image u OriginalFileName) cuyo CommandLine incluye una acción (' stop ', ' pause ', ' delete ', '.delete()', 'Stop-Service ', 'Remove-Service ' o 'config' con 'start=disabled') y el nombre de un servicio sensible, como WinDefend, Sophos, Veeam, VSS, MSSQL o SentinelAgent.
es.why_it_matters: Detener la protección de endpoint, los backups o las instantáneas de volumen le quita al defensor visibilidad y capacidad de recuperación. Las bases de datos se detienen para liberar archivos antes de cifrarlos. Corresponde a ATT&CK T1489 (Service Stop) y al debilitamiento de defensas.
triage_steps: Revise CommandLine: identifique la acción (stop, delete, start=disabled) y el servicio afectado; anote si hay varios servicios o un /y forzado.
Revise ParentImage y la cadena de procesos: ¿lo lanzó un .bat, cmd.exe, PsExec, una tarea programada o un agente de gestión conocido?
Identifique el usuario y el logon: ¿es una cuenta de administración esperada o una cuenta de servicio o de dominio inusual?
Pivotee en el mismo host +/- 15 minutos: busque muchas detenciones seguidas, vssadmin o wbadmin delete, bcdedit, wevtutil cl o cambios en Defender.
Busque el mismo CommandLine o el mismo padre en otros hosts; una ejecución masiva casi simultánea indica despliegue de ransomware.
Confirme el estado del servicio y del agente de seguridad (eventos 7036/7040 del System log, consola EDR) y si dejó de reportar.
Compruebe si existe un ticket de cambio, una actualización o una desinstalación planificada del producto afectado.
Revise alertas previas del host y del usuario: acceso remoto, volcado de credenciales o movimiento lateral.
false_positives: Administradores que detienen o deshabilitan servicios para actualizar o desinstalar antivirus, backup o bases de datos.
Instaladores y scripts de despliegue (SCCM, Intune, RMM) que detienen el servicio del producto durante el upgrade.
Ventanas de mantenimiento de SQL Server, Exchange o IIS que detienen servicios con scripts programados.
Limpieza de un producto de seguridad durante una migración de proveedor.
response_steps: Si no hay cambio autorizado, aísle el host desde el EDR o la red y conserve evidencia antes de reiniciar.
Deshabilite o restablezca la credencial usada y revise sus sesiones activas en otros equipos.
Restaure y vuelva a habilitar los servicios de seguridad y backup afectados; verifique que reporten a consola.
Busque y elimine el script, la tarea programada o el binario que lanzó el comando, y haga barridos por el mismo hash en el entorno.
Valide la integridad de los backups y las instantáneas antes de recuperar; si es benigno, agregue un filtro por ParentImage y documente.
es.severity_rationale: El nivel high se justifica porque detener la seguridad o los backups es un precursor directo del ransomware, aunque las tareas administrativas legítimas exigen verificarlo.

en.summary: net, sc, PowerShell, wmic or PsService was used to stop, pause, disable or delete a critical service such as antivirus, EDR, backup, database or VSS. Ransomware scripts commonly do this before encryption.
en.what_it_detects: Process creation of net.exe, net1.exe, sc.exe, wmic.exe, PsService, powershell.exe, pwsh.exe or PowerShell ISE (matched by Image or OriginalFileName). The CommandLine must contain an action (' stop ', ' pause ', ' delete ', '.delete()', 'Stop-Service ', 'Remove-Service ', or 'config' plus 'start=disabled') and the name of a sensitive service such as WinDefend, Sophos, Veeam, VSS, MSSQL or SentinelAgent.
en.why_it_matters: Stopping endpoint protection, backups or shadow copies blinds defenders and removes recovery options. Attackers stop databases to release locked files before encrypting them. This maps to ATT&CK T1489 (Service Stop) and defense impairment.
triage_steps: Read CommandLine: note the action (stop, delete, start=disabled), the targeted service, whether several services are hit and whether /y forces the change.
Check ParentImage and the process tree: was it a .bat file, cmd.exe, PsExec, a scheduled task or a known management agent?
Identify the user and logon session: is it an expected admin account or an unusual service or domain account?
Pivot on the same host +/- 15 minutes for bursts of service stops, vssadmin or wbadmin delete, bcdedit, wevtutil cl or Defender changes.
Search other hosts for the same CommandLine or parent; near-simultaneous execution across many hosts suggests ransomware deployment.
Confirm the service and security agent state with System events 7036/7040 and the EDR console, and check whether the agent stopped reporting.
Check for a change ticket, upgrade or planned uninstall of the affected product.
Review earlier alerts for the host and user, such as remote access, credential dumping or lateral movement.
false_positives: Administrators stopping or disabling services to upgrade or uninstall antivirus, backup or database software.
Installers and deployment scripts (SCCM, Intune, RMM) that stop the product's service during an upgrade.
Scheduled maintenance scripts for SQL Server, Exchange or IIS that stop services.
Removing a security product during a vendor migration.
response_steps: If no authorized change exists, isolate the host through EDR or the network and preserve evidence before rebooting.
Disable or reset the credential used and review its active sessions on other machines.
Restart and re-enable the affected security and backup services, then confirm they report to their consoles.
Find and remove the launching script, scheduled task or binary, and sweep the environment for the same hash.
Check that backups and shadow copies are intact before recovery. If the activity was benign, add a ParentImage filter and document it.
en.severity_rationale: High fits because stopping security or backup services directly precedes ransomware, but legitimate admin work means each alert still needs to be verified.

positive.description: net.exe launched from a batch script stops Windows Defender with /y
sc.exe disables the Volume Shadow Copy service

negative.description: sc.exe only queries the Defender service status, so no stop, delete or disable action is present
net.exe stops the Print Spooler, which is not on the rule's service list
